China's grip on rare-earths mining has slipped from about 90% a decade ago to roughly two-thirds today, as the West races to build alternatives.

The real chokepoint is processing. China still refines around 90% of the world's rare earths, and it used export controls last year to prove the leverage. Rebuilding a supply chain outside China is a decade-long project, a slow structural tailwind for Western critical-minerals miners, not a quick trade.

tweets.text:
The US 10-year yield is back near its highest since 2007, pushing 5%.

Set aside the day's headlines. The bigger message is that the bond market wants a lot more to fund a government that never stops borrowing. Even with the Fed's printer running, investors demand a 2007-level yield to hold US debt. A 5% risk-free rate reprices everything above it: stocks, housing, and the government's own interest bill, which only grows the deficit it is trying to fund.

🚨 Germany’s industrial competitiveness index fell from 21 in 2024 to just 3 in 2026. When almost every major industrial sector deteriorates at the same time, it means the problem looks much more structural.

🇩🇪🇨🇳 Germany probably had one of the best suited economic models to the world of the 1990s and 2000s with competitive energy, high-end manufacturing, a powerful Mittelstand, premium automotive brands, chemicals, machinery, and a China that was a huge customer. Now, China has become a direct competitor in the sectors where Germany used to dominate.

⚠️ However, reducing Germany’s problem to China and energy would be too easy. Bureaucracy, slow administrative processes, ageing demographics, past underinvestment in parts of the country’s infrastructure and weak productivity growth are progressively hurting the country. Another important mistake to avoid is that Germany could perfectly experience an economic rebound in 2026-2027 while continuing to lose industrial competitiveness as GDP can be supported by public spending, defence, infrastructure or simply a cyclical recovery.

Germany is not finished as it still has outstanding engineers, industrial clusters, world-class companies and enormous know-how, but its old economic model is clearly reaching its limits. A change is needed.

*Bloomberg link: https://t.co/nuUIiNaI88

🚨 The 10-year OAT-Bund spread is now approaching 120 basis points, a level not seen since the euro-area debt crisis.

🇫🇷 France is currently being hit by two shocks at the same time. Long-term yields are rising everywhere but France is also underperforming Germany which means its own risk premium is rising on top of that. The European risk-free rate is going up AND investors are asking for an additional premium to hold French debt because the fiscal backdrop is frankly poor.

📈 French public debt has now reached roughly €3.6 trillion, or 119% of GDP, while the government still needs to issue huge amounts of debt. France is expected to raise around €340 billion of medium and long-term debt in 2027, with the annual interest bill already projected at close to €73 billion.

🏠 This terrific situation does not stay confined to sovereign bonds. Government yields gradually feed into the entire economy (corporate funding, bank financing, mortgages and asset valuations) and real estate is a perfect example. The higher the return investors demand, the lower the theoretical value of an asset becomes, even if rents do not move.

Markets are starting to make France pay a much higher price for its fiscal imbalances.

*Bloomberg link: https://t.co/ybTCDXn0aj
